newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's ex-communist president urges forgiveness.
newsitem.headline: Poland's ex-communist president urges forgiveness.

text.p: Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski, once a senior communist, quoted Pope John Paul in urging Poles in a new year message to abandon thoughts of revenge for the wrongs of the communist era.
In a televised address, Kwasniewski recognised that many Poles in the past had suffered wrongs which could not be smoothed over and should be redressed as far as possible.
But he said it was vital to act on the words of the Polish- born Pontiff who had written: "The deadly routine of revenge must give way to the liberating innovation of forgiveness."

Kwasniewski, who beat his predecessor, former Solidarity chief Lech Walesa in elections a year ago, sees compromise between ex-communists and those who struggled for democracy before the 1989 fall of the old system as key goals.

His calls have assumed a new urgency since the Solidarity union gathered centre-right parties in a strong new grouping to challenge the co-ruling Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) of ex-communists at parliamentary elections in 1997.
The Solidarity campaign is likely to focus in part on seeking justice for communist period misdeeds.

Solidarity charges that while Kwasniewski talks of reconciliation, his camp has failed to bring culprits to book for past human rights abuses and has ensured that old communists have garnered an unfair share of Poland's wealth.
"It is up to each of us in the New Year, whether there will be more work and cooperation in Poland, dialogue and compromise, or negligence, feuds and time-wasting," he said.
